The vulnerability is a one-click attack that requires an authenticated admin to click a link that sends a malicious REST API request to create the account.

infosec.title: Containers Are No Longer a Security Boundary
infosec.summary: The traditional view of containers as a strong security and isolation mechanism is being eroded by the plethora of kernel vulnerabilities being uncovered. This article explains how a recent vulnerability in the AF_UNIX subsystem can be leveraged by attackers for container escapes. The authors recommend moving untrusted workloads to MicroVMs like Firecracker or Kata Containers for untrusted workloads.

infosec.title: From Exposure to Lockdown: How AWS Neutralizes Compromised IAM Credentials through Managed Policies
infosec.summary: AWS automatically attaches the AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV3 managed policy to an exposed IAM user within 10 seconds of a public GitHub push, with the CloudTrail AttachUserPolicy event misleadingly attributed to the victim's IAM user rather than to AWS automation. Each policy version tracked real-world attack evolution, with permissions added to block Lambda-based cryptomining, S3 data deletion for extortion, and Bedrock API abuse after Permiso's research exposed unauthorized InvokeModel calls. Security teams should alert on unexpected AttachUserPolicy events in CloudTrail, treat the quarantine event as confirmation of active key exposure rather than as resolution, and rotate all affected credentials before removing the policy.

infosec.title: PolinRider is A/B Testing its Way Past Your Detections
infosec.summary: DPRK's PolinRider malware spread through GitHub organizations by force-pushing rewritten commits from infected developers' machines, planting VS Code folderOpen tasks that run an obfuscated JavaScript payload disguised as fa-solid-400/500/900.woff2 and, since September 28, fa-solid-300.llf. OpenSourceMalware traced 853 force-pushes across three Binary-Mindz repos and found variants with different paths, obfuscators, and C2-reported build markers running in parallel, which it reads as deliberate A/B testing, while copied author dates and reused commit messages quietly reverted three cleanup attempts. Defenders should flag fake fonts by file content rather than name, scan every branch through bare clones, audit force-push activity logs, and enforce force-push blocking and signed commits on all branches.

infosec.title: House of Apple 2 on modern glibc
infosec.summary: This walkthrough breaks down House of Apple 2, a glibc FSOP technique that bypasses the vtable validation added in newer glibc. It points a FILE structure's vtable to legitimate wide-character stream code, which then dispatches to a second vtable that glibc does not range-check. Step by step in GDB, the author turns that unchecked indirect call into an arbitrary call, pivots the stack, and runs a ROP chain to a shell. The technique still works cleanly on glibc 2.43 (Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44). Exact offsets and gadgets vary between builds, but the underlying control-flow trick remains the same.

infosec.title: Sender spoofing in Proton Mail via display-name homograph
infosec.summary: Proton Mail's web interface can show a forged sender that looks identical to a real one. The attacker sets a display name containing an address-shaped string like sundar@gmaiI[.]com where the capital I matches lowercase l in the default UI font. Messages from domains without DMARC arrive in the inbox with no authentication banner, even when SPF fails. A Reply-To header can route responses to an attacker's address without showing it unless the user expands headers, and the spoofed sender also appears unchanged in macOS desktop notifications, outside the app interface. The issue was reported in February 2025, confirmed and bounty-awarded in April 2025, and can still be reproduced as of September 2026.

With shadcn and Tailwind v4, the key steps are an entry file with type definitions, a compiled stylesheet with safelisted layout utilities, fonts listed in extraFonts, and a conventions file. Storybook is optional, but it provides the reference that makes the sync verifiable.

design.title: Google has the best AI money can buy. Its products still feel broken

The deeper problem may be organizational: weak feedback loops between product teams and real users can produce fragmented features optimized for internal goals rather than actual workflows. For teams integrating AI, the key is to distinguish surfaces where occasional mistakes are acceptable from those where accuracy is fundamental, while preserving direct user feedback and making uncertainty visible.

design.title: Launch fast. Design beautifully with Framer. Now with Agents to make every step of the process effortless
design.summary: Framer is a pro website builder trusted by companies like Miro and Perplexity. With AI agents built into the canvas, teams can design pages, manage content, write copy, add SEO, and audit for issues. All without leaving the tool. Agents bring speed and scale; you bring the taste. Launch your site today

design.title: Free Chrome Screen Recorder with Cursor Zoom
design.summary: Screen capture with automatic cursor zoom, panning, and a built-in screen recording editor.

design.title: Your Pocket Film Camera
design.summary: Lightmeter captures natural and raw photos with authentic film looks. Zero-AI processing, no HDR. Natural colors, authentic grains.

design.title: AI Canvas for Real Design Work
design.summary: Generate, edit, and scale on-brand visuals in one workspace for marketing teams, ecommerce brands, and creative agencies.

design.title: MOKSi gives GiftTrees the confidence to be both good and profitable
design.summary: GiftTrees worked with MOKSi to reposition itself as a profitable business that creates positive environmental and social impact, centered on the proposition “impact made easy” and an intentionally upbeat, anti-guilt tone. The refreshed identity combines a leaf-and-bow logo, expressive typography, green with vibrant purple, orange, and red, and positive imagery to distinguish the company from traditional charity and sustainability branding. The result gives GiftTrees a clearer way to unite people, planet, and profit while supporting its ambition to scale from more than five million trees planted toward one billion.

design.title: Inca Kola rebrands as the world's other cola war heats up
design.summary: Inca Kola simplified its identity in 2016 by removing elements such as Peru's silhouette and its founding date, creating a cleaner, more modern logo but prompting criticism that the brand is losing some of its distinctly Peruvian character. Rather than relying on explicit national symbols, the new system emphasizes belonging through imagery of social gatherings and food, while turning the logo's distinctive shape into a flexible framing device. The identity also expands into sound with a four-note mnemonic created from traditional glass cola bottles, reinforcing familiar brand associations while modernizing the overall experience.

design.title: When Chat is the Wrong UI
design.summary: Chat has stayed the default way to work with AI for three years, but it suits people who don't know what they want, not those who do. In the GitHub Copilot app, a canvas is a small full-stack application, with no browser chrome, that talks back and forth with the agent. Examples include a playable Connect 4 game, a local package manager, and a workflow tool that automates research and planning so a developer can step back.

design.title: Easter Eggs in Product Design & Web Design
design.summary: Hidden features and secret interactions make a product feel delightful and memorable, tapping into the dopamine hit of discovering something unexpected.

design.title: The Death of Web Development Education
design.summary: Generative AI has gutted the market for web-development education.

marketing.title: Webinar on Oct 7th: How Corinthia Hotels uses AI agents to personalize at scale
marketing.summary: 96% of brands struggle to execute personalization at scale. Corinthia Hotels is not one of them. They built a 7-agent AI system on Optimizely that maps 76 behavioral signals to 6,384 content variants across 5 personas and 14 lifecycle stages. 100% brand approval rate. 150+ hours saved. Zero PII in the AI layer. Zero extra headcount. On October 7th , Emily Jewell, Senior Global Head of Marketing at Corinthia Hotels, walks you through the full system live — including two demos and a Q&A exclusive to attendees. 🏨 It's free. Register now →

marketing.title: Convenience or discovery: Which mission will your store serve?
marketing.summary: AI is splitting physical retail into two distinct missions. Convenience stores should reduce friction with easy navigation and reactive service. Discovery stores should drive dwell time through immersive experiences and specialized associates. More than 90% of consumers prioritize locations that fit their daily routines, while 78% cite product testing and 76% cite product guidance as drivers of discovery visits.

marketing.title: Workers are warming up to AI - but Gen Z remains skeptical
marketing.summary: AI confidence is growing across the workforce, with 53% of US workers saying AI makes them more efficient. Gen Z remains more hesitant. Only 38% plan to build AI skills in the next 6 months, while 52% are nervous about AI's impact on their jobs. At the same time, AI literacy is becoming more valuable in the workplace. LinkedIn finds it is associated with stronger hiring and promotion outcomes for Gen Z.

marketing.title: Audit if your FAQ is discoverable by search engines and LLMs
marketing.summary: FAQs can improve visibility in search and AI systems only if the content is present in the page source when it loads. Many FAQ components hide their text until a user clicks to expand them, which means search engines and LLMs may not access the content by default. Use Chrome DevTools to check whether FAQ text remains discoverable after a page reload.

marketing.title: ChatGPT reads your YouTube description, not your transcript
marketing.summary: Treat YouTube descriptions like landing pages for AI search. ChatGPT can retrieve a video's title, metadata, and full description, but not its transcript. That makes the description a key source for understanding the video. Include relevant terms and clear context. Use structured sections and timecodes so ChatGPT can understand what the video covers and where specific topics appear.

marketing.title: There is no AEO algorithm to hack
marketing.summary: AEO is not an SEO ranking game with factors to reverse engineer. AI visibility depends on whether a brand is clearly associated with a category and supported by credible evidence. Fix positioning gaps and answer real buyer questions. Build comparison content that helps buyers evaluate vendors. Strengthen third-party corroboration instead of manufacturing mentions. Then track commercial prompts and connect AI visibility to buyer conversations and pipeline, not just brand mentions.

marketing.title: AI makes it dangerously easy to scale a bad idea.
marketing.summary: Gather builds a simulation of your customers from real interviews. Run strategy simulation, test messaging, positioning, pricing, explore why buyers choose competitors, and get insights instantly. Trusted by Datadog, Fortinet, Cyera, Bagel Brands, Staples, and others. Try a customer simulation →

marketing.title: Almost nobody gets XML sitemaps right
marketing.summary: XML sitemaps tell search engines which URLs a site wants in search results. They should contain canonical, working URLs that the site wants indexed. Google attempts to crawl each URL as listed, so redirects, errors, noindex pages, or conflicting canonicals make the sitemap less useful and can waste crawl activity. Missing or repeated ‘lastmod' dates can be acceptable. Fields like ‘priority' and ‘changefreq' are ignored by Google.

marketing.title: Does Reddit have an astroturfing problem?
marketing.summary: Reddit is often treated as a source of unbiased product advice. However, some buying recommendations are unusually concentrated among a small group of accounts. The top 5% of brand-heavy accounts produced 11.3% of knife recommendations, versus 7.9% expected by chance. For three brands, that share reached 20% to 31%. This could indicate astroturfing, where paid accounts create the appearance of organic recommendations, but their histories looked more like genuine fans.

marketing.title: Dissecting why Canva is partnering with Jio
marketing.summary: Canva is using Jio's 524.4M customers to tackle a freemium problem. Many casual users get enough value from Free to justify paying for Pro. Bundling Pro with Jio plans lets users experience premium features without making a separate purchase. The real test is what happens after the bundle ends. Canva needs to see whether users build habits around Pro and become willing to pay for it.

marketing.title: The usefulness of attribution for AI Search
marketing.summary: AI is making click-based attribution less useful as discovery increasingly happens through AI answers that never generate a website visit. Treat attribution as one imperfect signal rather than a definitive measure of channel value. Triangulate exposure, behavioral, and business metrics such as AI Share of Voice and CRM data. Use incrementality testing where possible to measure causal impact, especially for activities that attribution cannot capture.

marketing.title: Wendy's Drops an Emo Album: “Songs to Listen to in a Wendy's Parking Lot”
marketing.summary: Wendy's dropped a full emo EP for late-night food runs.

marketing.title: The "Are you still that person?" trick
marketing.summary: Use identity-based emails to re-engage churned customers and dead leads.

crypto.title: Strategy Proposes Daily Dividends to Bring STRC Back Toward $100
crypto.summary: Strategy is seeking shareholder approval on October 28 to implement daily dividend accrual across its four US-listed preferred stocks (STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD), a timing-only change that leaves existing dividend rates and total payouts unchanged. STRC has traded below its $100 stated value since May, fell to $71 during bitcoin's June correction, and has failed to recover to par despite a 12% annual yield and roughly $1 billion in preferred share repurchases. Daily accrual, paid each subsequent business day, is designed to attract income-focused investors by eliminating reinvestment gaps between distributions and dampening price swings around payment dates. Strategy holds 846,000 BTC acquired at an average cost of $75,416 per coin, meaning bitcoin price moves feed through to these preferred instruments, and the June drawdown in BTC explains STRC's drop below par.

crypto.title: Bitget starts phased withdrawal resumption following $388 million exploit
crypto.summary: Bitget began restoring withdrawals in stages after an exploit on September 24 drained ~$388 million from its hot and warm wallets, the largest reported crypto theft this year. BTC withdrawals resumed September 29 at 8 AM UTC, with ETH following September 29, USDT on September 30, and all remaining assets, fiat, and P2P by October 2. Bitget said an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to obtain internal credentials and send fraudulent withdrawal commands, bypassing risk controls. Private keys, cold wallets, and user balances weren't affected. Losses will be fully covered by Bitget's 5,500 BTC User Protection Fund. Bitget said it suspects the attackers were "sophisticated" and "state-backed," pointing to North Korea.

crypto.title: Solana Upgrade That Could Cut Finality from 12.8s to 150ms
crypto.summary: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade has moved to public testnet, replacing TowerBFT with a new consensus protocol called Votor that reduces transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. Votor replaces on-chain vote accumulation across 32 slots with direct validator-to-validator messaging that settles in one or two rounds, requiring no changes to wallets or user-facing transaction flows. The rollout requires Agave 4.3 validator software, while Firedancer and Frankendancer clients do not yet support the upgrade, and a tentative mainnet date of September 28 has not been confirmed. The finality reduction would cut the hold periods exchanges impose before crediting deposits, the wait bridges require before releasing cross-chain funds, and the confirmation delays merchants currently face.

crypto.title: The Cryptographic World Computer
crypto.summary: Vitalik Buterin's new paper reframes Ethereum's post-Hegota trajectory as a shift from blockchain to "cryptographic world computer," a hybrid architecture combining traditional consensus with modern cryptography to support properties no pure blockchain can deliver. The roadmap covers FOCIL for censorship resistance, EIP-8288, Lean consensus, state management improvements, and advanced mempool upgrades including transaction privacy. The paper also raises obfuscation as a longer-term primitive that could expand what on-chain computation can offer. Buterin structures the argument through a section-by-section comparison of the Bitcoin whitepaper against Ethereum's 2015, 2025, and 2030 states to show how far the design goals have diverged from their origins.

crypto.title: Why AI agents could make bank runs faster and more violent
crypto.summary: The real story isn't an imminent agentic bank run but the collapse of cheap bank funding broadly, which will compress return on equity for banks and brokers like Schwab and IBKR that rely on idle sweep-account cash. When agentic bank runs do happen, they'll be faster and more violent than human ones like SVB's, because AI agents have much lower behavioral diversity than humans.

crypto.title: Why Ethereum's L1 State Ownership Is Non-Negotiable
crypto.summary: Offchain computation with onchain proofs creates a cryptographic bulletin board, not a world computer. Ethereum Foundation researcher Barnabé Monnot draws the line at state ownership: Ethereum's network effects derive from its liquidity and accessible onchain state, which allow permissionless actions like liquidations without dependence on brittle third-party APIs or centralized servers. Composability scales with how granular and accessible onchain state is, and offchain state resolution fractures that permissionless composability. The Ethlabs vision follows: L1 as liquidity hub and secure asset layer, with L2s as differentiated state neighborhoods that reinforce and extend L1 network effects while absorbing the offchain economy.

crypto.title: Circle's Tazapay acquisition is really about buying an off-ramp for USDC
crypto.summary: By tracing on-chain flows behind Circle's September 8 announcement to acquire Tazapay, a Singapore B2B cross-border payments firm, it seems about a third of Tazapay's payout business is already funded in USDC (up from under 10% in June), with monthly redemptions into Circle hitting $562 million in the first 25 days of September. Circle isn't buying a future USDC channel but a client that already burns over half a billion dollars of USDC monthly through Circle Mint plus the fiat off-ramp rails on the other side, since Tazapay's product is one-directional (stablecoin in, fiat out) with almost no on-chain revenue (2 basis points). The real business is the FX spread at the off-ramp, not the blockchain layer itself.

crypto.title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Holds Bitcoin in a Coinbase Wallet
crypto.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth disclosed Bitcoin holdings of $16,000-$65,000 in a Coinbase wallet via his 2025 OGE financial disclosure, split across two capital gains entries. The filing shows no Bitcoin transactions above $1,000 during 2025, indicating Hegseth held a passive position throughout the year. His exposure is modest compared to President Trump's June filing, which reported over $50 million in Bitcoin and $1.2 billion in crypto-related earnings. The disclosures from multiple senior US executive branch officials mark Bitcoin ownership as established at the cabinet level, with Coinbase serving as the disclosed custodian for at least one sitting secretary.

crypto.summary: Degenerate-adjacent branding has migrated from fringe meme culture into mainstream DeFi and meme coin marketing.

crypto.summary: Binance Wallet now lets users pay gas fees directly in USDT on Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain, and TRON, removing the need to separately hold small amounts of ETH, SOL, BNB, or TRX just to move USDT already in the wallet.

crypto.title: Plasma One offers strong USD-EUR transfer rates
crypto.summary: In comparing USD-EUR transfer rates across platforms for sending $1,015, Plasma One gave recipients €890.45, only about 0.14% below the Google reference rate, beating RedotPay (€888.63), Wise (€886.90), Western Union (€885.64), Instarem (€884.77), and MoneyGram (€882.35).

it.title: Live Oct 6: What IT leaders need to know about governing at the speed of AI, with Forrester
it.summary: AI made building software easier, and now more of it is entering the enterprise than IT has ever had to govern. Keeping up takes new thinking on security, access, and oversight, built for software created faster and by more people than ever. On October 6, join Tines and Forrester for a candid conversation on why decision velocity is becoming IT's new differentiator, and what it means to govern outcomes rather than just oversee systems. You'll learn how IT accountability is shifting from delivery to outcomes, and practical ways to position your team now for the next five years of AI-driven change. Save your seat here.

it.title: Over 16,000 Supabase databases expose PII, passwords, auth tokens
it.summary: UpGuard identified more than 16,000 Supabase databases exposing readable tables. Analysis of their schemas indicated that more than half could expose personal information, with smaller subsets potentially exposing passwords or authentication tokens. The issue is misconfigured access controls rather than a newly discovered platform vulnerability, reinforcing the need for database authorization, exposure testing, and clear ownership of internally built tools.

it.title: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations
it.summary: Microsoft has paused optional update KB5002907 after reports that it left some Office 2016 and 2019 installations unlicensed or, rarely, removed. Its recovery guidance is to reactivate or reinstall the affected product. Importantly, the update makes no changes where Microsoft 365 Apps updates are managed through Group Policy or Cloud Update. Support teams should check update history before treating unexpected licensing tickets as subscription or account problems.

it.title: The SaaSpocalypse that wasn't, with Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes
it.summary: In this Decoder interview, Mike Cannon-Brookes explains why Atlassian combined internal IT and AI enablement under its people leadership: employee adoption and changes to business systems are tightly connected. He also argues that AI will change SaaS workflows without eliminating the need for structured systems and human judgment. For CIOs, the interesting question is who owns the combined work of employee enablement, system integration, and AI cost management, rather than treating each as a separate rollout.

it.title: 7 reasons IT managers fail to exceed your expectations
it.summary: Promoting a strong technologist does not automatically prepare them to manage people, business relationships, or competing operational priorities. This piece examines unclear expectations, insufficient leadership development, and the tendency to reward technical output without developing management skills. It is a useful operating-model check for CIOs overseeing support, infrastructure, SaaS, and business systems: define what managers own, coach them on business outcomes, and provide advancement paths for specialists who should remain individual contributors.

it.title: Workday Launches Total Benefits, Bringing Health, Wealth, and Wellbeing Support Together in One Place
it.summary: Workday has announced Total Benefits, combining benefits-provider integrations, administration services, and employee guidance in one offering. Workday Wellness is now available to US customers, while benefits guidance through its Self-Service Agent is expected to become generally available in October. Evaluation should cover provider compatibility, sensitive employee-data sharing, and whether the new workflows can replace existing portals and manual administration rather than simply adding another layer.

it.title: Anthropic turns Claude into an AI marketplace with 2,000+ plugins and connectors
it.summary: Anthropic's marketplace brings together more than 2,000 plugins and connectors, partner-built agents, and services, with eligible partner software purchasable using a portion of committed Anthropic spending. For an internal AI platform team, the significant change is the growing catalog of connections between assistants and business systems, along with another procurement channel to manage. Marketplace availability should not replace reviewing permissions, data access, integration ownership, and how access will be removed when someone leaves.

it.title: How to Disable BitLocker in Windows 11 (And When You Shouldn't)
it.summary: Disabling BitLocker starts decrypting the drive, while suspending protection leaves the data encrypted but temporarily makes the encryption key accessible. This walkthrough explains the distinction and why short-term firmware maintenance or troubleshooting often calls for suspension rather than removing encryption entirely. The operational takeaway is to make resuming and verifying protection part of the endpoint maintenance runbook, not optional cleanup after the support ticket closes.

it.title: Microsoft adds pay-as-you-go pricing for extra OneDrive storage
it.summary: Microsoft 365 customers can now use consumption-based billing when users exceed their licensed OneDrive storage instead of purchasing additional capacity upfront. Admins choose which users are eligible and can set budgets and alerts. Additional storage costs $0.20/GB/month. Enterprise SaaS is shifting toward usage-based pricing, giving IT more flexibility but also making cost monitoring part of day-to-day platform management.

it.title: New Google Meet 'Take notes for me' settings for admins and end users take effect September 29th
it.summary: Google will begin applying new automatic-note settings on September 29.

it.title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
it.summary: Cloudflare says it completed remediation of a cross-tenant storage-reuse flaw affecting Containers and Sandboxes by September 19, found no evidence of malicious exploitation in available telemetry, and requires no customer-side action.
